title: Subscriber health metrics translation guide
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note translates infra/telemetry metrics (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate) into customer-facing QBR fields and renewal signals. Intended audience: Customer Success managers preparing QBR slides, Solutions Eng for renewal conversations, and SRE/observability owners who supply the numbers.

Format notes (how to read figures we present)
- Measurement windows: default = last 30 days for trends, 7-day rolling for recent anomalies.
- Aggregates we prefer: median (p50) and p95 for latency; uptime as monthly availability; cost/token as average over last 30 days; cache hit rate as weighted by request volume.
- Alert/variance calls: flag when p95 latency increases >25% month-over-month or cache hit rate drops >10% absolute.

Definitions (customer-facing wording + technical calc)
1) Latency (customer view): Typical response time experienced by your app and spikes that affect UX.
   - Technical: p50, p95 of end-to-end generation latency (API gateway receive -> final token emitted).
   - Query window for QBR: 30d median and 30d p95. Also include 7d p95 for recent incidents.
   - Calculation: median and 95th percentile of per-request total millis from Prometheus histogram `api_response_latency_ms_bucket` filtered by customer_id.

2) Uptime / Availability (customer view): Percent of time the service met success criteria (no 5xx, below latency SLO).
   - Technical: (successful_requests / total_requests) * 100 over the month, where successful excludes 5xx and timeouts. Optionally include SLO-compliant windows: % of requests under configured latency SLO at p95.
   - Calculation: derived from logs + synthetic checks (synthetic check pass rate weighted 30%).

3) Cost per token (customer view): Effective cost for tokens consumed by your product (in USD/token) — helps commercial discussions and cost-savings playbook.
   - Technical: total billed spend for model+inference / total tokens billed (input+output) over window. Break out by model family (e.g., Llama-2-70B-int8 vs small chat) and path (streamed vs batched).
   - Calculation: sum(cost_line_items where customer_id) / sum(tokens where customer_id). Use billing export as gold source.

4) Cache hit rate (customer view): Fraction of requests satisfied from prefix/KV cache vs fresh model compute — measures efficiency and latency improvement.
   - Technical: hits / (hits + misses) over window, where hits are cache-serve events at router/runtime. Weight by tokens returned (since a hit on a long completion matters more).
   - Calculation: (sum(cache_hit_tokens) / sum(total_tokens_served)) * 100. Also present simple hits/(hits+misses) for behavioral analysis.

Mapping to renewal signals (example thresholds for early-warning)
- Low risk (green): p95 latency < 450ms, uptime >= 99.95%, cost/token within +/-10% of baseline, cache hit rate >= 65%
- Medium risk (amber): p95 latency 450-900ms or uptime 99.9-99.95% or cache hit 45-65% or cost/token +10-30% above baseline
- High risk (red): p95 latency >900ms or uptime <99.9% or cache hit <45% or cost/token >30% above baseline
Use these for renewal prep triage; thresholds should be tuned per customer SLA tier and product surface.

Sample KPI table (paste into QBR slide table — values are examples):
Customer | p50 latency (ms) | p95 latency (ms) | Uptime (%) | Cost/token ($e-3) | Cache hit (%) | Trend (30d)
ACME Co | 120 | 380 | 99.98 | 0.0045 | 72 | stable
FintechX | 240 | 1120 | 99.88 | 0.0070 | 38 | degrading (cache drop)
RetailMart | 95 | 310 | 99.995 | 0.0039 | 81 | improving (quantize)

Operational notes (what to ask SRE / observability):
- Concrete queries: provide PromQL snippets and billing query IDs in the ticket. Example PromQL for p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(api_response_latency_ms_bucket{customer_id=~"%s"}[5m])) by (le))
- For cache hit tokens: check runtime metric `cache_serve_tokens_total{customer_id}` and `total_tokens_served{customer_id}`
- Billing joins: prefer daily exported billing table `billing_export.customer_usage` and partition by day for accurate cost/token.

QBR narrative guidance (how CSM should present it):
- Leading with impact: "Over the last 30 days ACME's p95 latency improved 20%, driven by a 12% cache hit increase after we tuned prompts and enabled per-route cache TTLs."
- If risk: propose explicit remediation and ask for commit: e.g., "We recommend upgrading to dedicated capacity (predictable throughput) or enabling per-route caching TTL of 24h for FAQ flows. Estimated saving: ~22% of token cost."

Open questions / items to resolve:
- Agree canonical baseline period (default to prev-quarter median) for cost comparisons.
- How to handle multi-tenant models where model-level metrics cannot be filtered by customer id (fallback: estimate using per-route traffic proportions).
- Decide SLO templates per plan (startup vs enterprise).

Action items (owner tags):
- Samir: add PromQL snippets to shared playbook and validate for 3 sample customers. (due 2025-03-07)
- Lena: confirm billing export join keys with finance. (due 2025-03-05)
- Ava: draft QBR slide template using the sample KPI table and circulate. (due 2025-03-03)

References and quick links:
- Observability runbook (internal): CON-4321
- Billing export schema: https://bigquery.redwood.internal/billing_export
- Related infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/214

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep customer language non-technical; show 3 numbers max on the main slide.
- For renewal decks show both "trend" and "recommended action" column.
- Consider adding a small 1-line cost sensitivity analysis (if we change quantization or batching settings).

If you want, I can produce a 1-slide QBR template and a short Prometheus + billing snippet bundle to attach to this doc.
